newsitem.title: INDIA: Bayer India results fail to cheer market.
newsitem.headline: Bayer India results fail to cheer market.

text.p: Share prices of Bayer India Ltd eased on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday after the firm's 1996 results failed to cheer the market, dealers said.
Bayer India shares fell 50 rupees to 2,000 on the BSE.
The firm is the Indian subsidiary of German chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Bayer AG.
"We were expecting a better second half from higher kharif (winter crop) season sales," said an analyst at a brokerage.
The company is one of India's major agrochemicals makers.
Bayer India on Wednesday announced a net profit of 103.3 million rupees for calendar 1996, up from 30.0 million rupees during the nine months ended 31 December 1995.
The company had increased its field force and launched new products in the pharmaceuticals division.
Bayer India said the major contribution to the turnover came from agrochemicals, followed by rubber and health care business.
